subject: Admin activity evidence: compact ledger export, redaction options, and delivery plan
messages:
From: Lara Simmons <lsimmons@brightline-audit.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Patel <mpatel@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — admin activity exports (SIG / SOC2)

Hi Sean,

We're preparing the SIG/SOC2 evidence package for AcmeCloud and need the admin activity/audit log export details so we can confirm scope and sampling for the control set. Specifically can you provide the following:

- A short list of the canonical fields included in the admin-ledger export (examples: actor, action, resource, timestamp, request_id, ip, raw_payload?)
- Retention window and whether per-tenant retention can be shortened/extended for export slices
- Export formats you can deliver (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV) and if exports support gzip/zip compression
- Redaction/pseudonymization options for PII (which fields can be masked vs removed) and whether redaction is deterministic
- How exports are signed/verifiable (HMAC, signed manifest, KMS key options)
- Delivery options: SFTP, presigned S3, or transfer to customer-managed bucket + expected lead time for a full-scope export (~12 months)
- Any attachments or sample files you can share that mirror the payload we would receive

If possible, please attach a small sample export (one day or 1000 rows) and a sample signed manifest so our auditors can validate checksums and signatures. Acme's security team prefers presigned S3 with server-side encryption using a customer-managed key if that's supported.

Thanks — aim to include this in the package by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Lara Simmons
Senior Auditor, Brightline Assurance

Subject: Re: Evidence request — admin activity exports (SIG / SOC2)

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infra/runtime) and Grace (compliance) to validate the details and confirm samples. High-level answers up front so Acme has expectations:

- Fields: our compact admin ledger includes event_ts, tenant_id, actor_id (hashed by default), actor_role, actor_type (user/service), action_type, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, src_ip, user_agent, change_summary (structured delta), session_id, raw_event_blob (optional).
- Retention: default 365 days across hosted accounts. We can provide on‑demand snapshots for a requested window; per-tenant retention adjustment requires a Dedicated/Private arrangement or an approved exception for exports.
- Formats & compression: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and Parquet are available. We can gzip NDJSON or provide parquet + gzip. CSV export is supported for small scope exports but not recommended because of nested fields.
- Redaction: PII fields (email, phone, full_name) can be pseudonymized (deterministic hash) or redacted (removed). IP address redaction is supported as either truncated (/24) or removed. Redaction happens pre-export in a deterministic pipeline so auditors can validate pseudonyms across exports if requested.
- Signing: manifests are HMAC-SHA256 signed by a Redwood signing key; we can instead use a customer-provided KMS key to sign the manifest if Acme supplies a key ARN (AWS KMS) or an equivalent. Exports contain checksums (sha256) for each payload chunk.
- Delivery: presigned S3 or SFTP both supported. We also offer direct transfer to a customer-managed S3 bucket via cross-account replication when set up ahead of time.
- Lead time: small samples (<= 1000 rows) — 1–2 business days. Full 12‑month export — typical 5–10 business days depending on sampling/redaction and key exchange for CMK.

Karthik / Grace — please confirm the exact field names and suggest any protections we should call out to auditors (HSM/KMS details, manifest fields, chunking strategy). I'll prepare a sample export and manifest once you confirm.

Thanks,
Sean
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Evidence request — admin activity exports (SIG / SOC2)

Adding the technical specifics so Lara and Acme know exactly what we'll deliver. I'll keep this short and machine-readable friendly:

Export ledger canonical fields (exact names in export):
- event_ts (ISO-8601 UTC)
- tenant_id
- actor_id_pseud (sha256 hex, deterministic)
- actor_type
- actor_role
- action
- resource_type
- resource_id
- request_id
- src_ip (raw OR truncated OR removed — configured per export)
- user_agent
- change_summary (JSON string)
- session_id
- raw_event_blob (base64-encoded JSON; included only when requested)

Retention and sampling:
- Platform default retention: 365 days.
- On-demand snapshot exports are created per request; we snapshot the canonical ledger for the requested date range and freeze the artifacts (immutable).
- For PII-sensitive requests we recommend snapshot + deterministic pseudonymization to preserve referential integrity.

Formats, chunking, and checksums: 
- Output formats: Parquet (columnar, preferred for large exports) and NDJSON (gzip).
- Chunking: we typically chunk by 12-hour windows to keep objects < 2GB but can change to 24-hour if preferred.
- Each chunk includes a sha256 checksum in the manifest and a size field (bytes).
- Manifest fields: export_id, tenant_id, range_start, range_end, chunk_name, chunk_sha256, chunk_size, record_count, signed_by, signature_type, signature_value, manifest_creation_ts.

Signing and encryption: 
- Manifests are signed using Redwood's HSM-backed signing key by default (RSA PSS + SHA256).
- Alternative: customer-provided signing key via AWS KMS asymmetric key (we accept a key ARN and sign via KMS Sign API).
- Payload encryption: envelope encryption with a data key encrypted by either Redwood KMS or customer-provided KMS key. For presigned S3, we support SSE-C and SSE-KMS patterns as needed.

Redaction/pseudonymization details: 
- Pseudonymization is deterministic (sha256 with tenant-specific salt) so the same actor maps to the same pseudonym across exports.
- Field-level options: "keep", "mask", "remove".
- For auditors who need correlation but not raw PII, we recommend: keep tenant_id, actor_id_pseud, action, resource_type, request_id; mask email and phone; truncate IP to /24.

Delivery options & timeline: 
- Presigned S3: we will upload chunks to a Redwood staging bucket and provide presigned GET URLs valid for 7 days. Preferred for quick turnarounds.
- Direct cross-account S3: requires setting bucket policy and cross-account role (2–3 business days to configure).
- SFTP: available via managed transfer endpoint; can be slower depending on queue.

Example timeline for a 12-month scoped, redacted, signed export:
1) Kickoff and key exchange (CMK ARN, manifest signing choice): 1 business day to confirm.
2) Snapshot & preprocessing (redaction/pseudonymization): 2–4 business days depending on volume and redaction options.
3) Packaging, checksum/signature, upload, QA: 2–4 business days.

Total: 5–10 business days.

I've attached:
- sample_admin_export_20260512.parquet (1 day sample)
- audit_export_schema_v2.csv (field list + descriptions)
- manifest_example.json.sig (signed manifest example)

If Acme wants deterministic mapping to real user IDs for internal investigation, we can provide a sealed mapping file encrypted with their CMK with additional governance controls; that is an escalation and requires approvals.

Let me know if Lara wants the sample delivered to presigned S3 or we should put it on SFTP.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Lara / Mike — thanks for the patience and the clear ask. Attached you'll find the sample parquet, a CSV field spec, and a signed manifest example. Quick summary and next steps so we can move this into Acme's package: 

- What you'll get: a deterministic, pseudonymized Parquet export for the requested window (default chunking 12h), sha256 checksums per chunk, and a signed manifest (we used Redwood signing in the sample).
- Redaction defaults: email/phone masked, IP truncated to /24. If you want IP removed entirely or want deterministic hashing instead of masking, tell us and we'll configure that for the snapshot job.
- Delivery options: confirm presigned S3 (we will upload and share presigned GET URLs valid 7 days) OR provide a pre-configured cross-account bucket ARN and we will push objects there. Acme's preference for CMK encryption is supported — please provide the ARN for the KMS key and whether you want the manifest signed by Redwood or via your KMS.
- Timeline: once we have delivery method + manifest/signing choice, we'll produce the requested one‑day sample within 24 hours and the full 12‑month snapshot within 7 business days (assuming no special redaction escrow or sealed mapping).

Please confirm: 1) delivery preference (presigned S3 OR cross-account push OR SFTP), 2) CMK ARN (if using customer-managed encryption), and 3) whether Acme needs deterministic mapping to real IDs (this requires additional approvals).

If there are any other fields the auditors expect that aren't in the sample, call that out; we'll include them when we run the job.

Best,
Sean
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
